title: Manufacturing and Analytical Development for JLK-247 Gene Therapy
text:
Our project is focused on the development of a treatment for Sanfilippo Syndrome Type C, a fatal
neurodegenerative disorder of childhood, which has enormous health and socioeconomic impact on many
families and on the healthcare system. We will execute a 500 L manufacturing of JLK-247 gene therapy vector
for treatment of MPS IIIC patients. We intend to develop and commercialize the first specific therapy for this
indication.

title: Clonal Evolution and Immune Dysregulation in AML patients treated with Venetoclax and Azacitidine after Allogeneic Stem Cell Transplantation
text:
AML patients who relapse after allogeneic stem cell transplant have a dismal prognosis, with 1-year survival rate
of less than 20%. Understanding the mechanism of relapse, particularly through the study of clonal evolution on
single cell level in addition to immune related changes could inform post-transplant treatment strategies to
improve outcomes. In this project, we aim to analyze longitudinally collected samples from post-transplant AML
patients-who have enrolled on an ongoing phase II trial of venetoclax and azicitidine (NCT04128501) for relapse
prevention-specifically to identify a) genetic mutations contributing to disease resistance and monitor the
evolution of mutational patterns, b) the impact of venetoclax and azacitidine post-transplant therapy on anti-
leukemic immunity, particularly in the period preceding overt relapse.

title: A membrane fusion apparatus trailblazes measles virus spread in airway cells
text:
Measles virus is so contagious that eradication would require a global vaccination and booster rate exceeding
95%. By unraveling the mechanism of cell-to-cell spread in airway cells, we hope to better understand a vital
step that occurs prior to host-to-host transmission. Such information may bolster defenses against emerging
pathogens and help develop targeted outbreak intervention tactics in schools and healthcare settings.

title: Remote effects of focal hippocampal seizures on neocortical function
text:
Impaired function of the cerebral cortex and cognitive deficits have a large impact on quality of life in people
with temporal lobe epilepsy. Understanding the fundamental mechanisms of remote network impairment in
focal epilepsy may lead to novel surgical, neurostimulation, or pharmacologic therapies for this disorder.

title: Multi-level Mechanisms of Behavioral Activation Therapy for Adolescent Depression
text:
Behavioral Activation (BA) psychotherapy has emerged as a first-line treatment for adolescent depression, yet
the underlying neurobiological mechanisms of BA’s efficacy remain unclear. A fuller understanding of BA’s
targets of treatment engagement requires multiple assessments linking trajectories of behavioral and symptom
change with trajectories of change in these neural circuits over the course of therapy as opposed to just
pre/post comparisons. This study will provide insights that can be used to develop new treatment biomarkers,
inform BA treatment augmentation, further novel treatment development, and facilitate precision-based
psychotherapy interventions to more effectively treat this major public health problem.

title: FMRP regulation of mitochondria and metabolism in mammalian brain development
text:
The proposed work will fill a major gap of our knowledge in understanding function of FMRP in regulating
energy metabolism during human brain development. Such understanding is critical for better therapeutic
development for fragile X syndrome as well as other neurodevelopmental disorders including autism.

title: Engineering enhanced chimeric autoantibody receptor T cell therapy for Pemphigus Vulgaris
text:
Autoantibody-mediated diseases such as pemphigus vulgaris (PV) and myasthenia gravis (MG) remain life-
threatening and difficult to treat because current immunosuppressive strategies non-selectively deplete
protective immunity and carry high risks of infection. Building on early-phase clinical trials of DSG3- and MuSK-
CAAR T cells, which demonstrated safety but limited persistence and efficacy, this project will develop next-
generation CAAR T cells with improved receptor design, in vivo stimulation platforms, and orthogonal cytokine
support to overcome barriers of target scarcity and receptor instability. Successful completion will provide
transformative, antigen-specific therapies that selectively eliminate pathogenic B cells while preserving
protective immunity, setting the stage for clinical translation in PV and MG.

title: Harnessing Health Data Science capacity to strengthen evidence-based interventions, policy and response to  the HIV/AIDS Epidemic in Uganda (H-DATA)
text: This health data science training program leverages Uganda’s high-volume clinical cohorts and innovative healthcare delivery models to train scientists in advanced predictive analytics and machine learning for HIV control. By evaluating these decentralized care strategies in a data-dense environment, the program generates actionable insights directly translatable to American jurisdictions facing severe care-retention differentials, particularly within rural Southern and urban metropolitan areas with documented healthcare infrastructure deficits. Ultimately, this cross-continental partnership strengthens American public health by providing cost-effective, data-driven interventions to optimize domestic HIV prevention, enhance epidemic forecasting, and minimize systemic gaps in clinical care continuity.

title: Metabolic and genetic determinants of Mtb heterogeneity in disease, drug response, and resistance
text:
Metabolic and genetic determinants of Mtb heterogeneity in disease, drug response, and resistance
Co-Principal Investigators, Kyu Rhee and Branch Moody
Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb) generates genetic heterogeneity through chromosomal mutations, so the
genomes of Mtb specimens taken from patients are a genetic record of changes needed for Mtb adaptation to
survive and transmit in humans. Here we detect genes that control mycobacterial lipids and metabolites as a
crucial and now broadly surveyable aspect of Mtb physiology. This interdisciplinary research program will
define the genes that encode metabolites and lipids that are essential for Mtb infection, transmission,
persistence and drug resistance, so that we can design therapies to counter these crucial molecules.

title: Sex-Specific Genetic Drivers of Alzheimer's Disease Endophenotypes
text:
Two-thirds of Alzheimer’s disease (AD) cases are female, and research suggests that the disease affects male
and female brains in different ways. The goal of this project is to identify sex-specific genetic drivers of AD
neuropathology, neurodegeneration, and cognitive impairment. The identification of such genetic markers will
facilitate the development of personalized interventions that are tailored to the sex and neuropathology of the
individual.

title: Defining PRC1.1 as a gatekeeper of lineage plasticity and response to anti-GD2 therapy
text:
Epigenetic dysregulation is frequently observed in the disease pathology of pediatric cancers, including
neuroblastoma (NB), the most common extracranial solid tumor in pediatric patients. We’ve discovered that
adoption of a mesenchymal lineage is associated with loss of GD2 expression, resulting in resistance to anti-
GD2 therapy. This proposal outlines the targeting of PRC1.1 via inhibition of USP7 as a therapeutic
intervention to directly target neuroblastomas and restore the response to anti-GD2 therapy.
.

title: Mechanisms of sigma-factor-dependent transcriptional control in Mycobacterium tuberculosis
text:
Sigma-factors are critical protein components of the bacterial transcription machinery, reprograming the
transcriptome to adapt to different environmental cues and stresses encountered from the host. The primary
sigma-factor in Mycobacterium tuberculosis (Mtb), the causative bacterial agent of tuberculosis (TB), contains
an intrinsically disordered region (IDR) of unknown function. The proposed work will evaluate the structural
dynamics and function of this IDR, in effort to understand its role in Mtb transcriptional regulation and bacterial
resistance against the current primary antibiotic used to treat TB infections.

title: Systems analysis of mechanisms driving response to immunotherapy in clear cell cancers
text:
This administrative supplement addresses a tumor-associated macrophage signal newly
identiﬁed in our spatial and transcriptomic analyses of clear cell cancers, a ﬁnding not
anticipated when the parent grant was funded. We will adapt a recently published CRISPR
activation surfaceome screening approach to identify which immune-expressed ligands
drive this eCect on anti-tumor immunity. The work directly extends the parent grant Aim 3 to
validate causal drivers of immunotherapy response, providing functional evidence to
complement our computational and imaging-based ﬁndings within the current project
period.

title: Elucidating the Role of AIRE and Tumor Associated Aire-expressing Cells in Tumor Growth and Immune Evasion
text:
AIRE is required for maintaining tolerance in the thymus and periphery to prevent autoimmune diseases but
can also play a detrimental role by dampening immune responses against cancer. While deletion of thymic
AIRE expression has been shown to improve response to immunotherapy in certain cancers by allowing the
development of autoreactive T cells, whether extrathymic AIRE expression is involved in regulating anti-tumor
immune responses remains unknown. This proposal investigates the role of peripheral AIRE expression and
tumor associated Aire-expressing cells in tumor progression and immunity with the ultimate goal of improving
immunotherapy approaches for cancer treatment.

title: DP1 receptor signaling in aging-associated immune dysfunction in lung metastases
text: (PROJECT 2 – ZHENG) “DP1 receptor signaling in aging-associated immune dysfunction in lung metastases” Recent studies from our laboratory revealed that age-related anti-viral immune dysfunction in the respiratory tract is driven by the increased expression of an inducible phospholipase A2 group IID (PLA2G2D) enzyme and the prostaglandin D2 receptor, DP1. Specifically, we discovered that age-related mortality in SARs- CoV2-infected mice were largely reversed in both PLA2G2D-/- and DP1-/- mice as a consequence of enhanced lung dendritic cell (DC) mediated anti-viral-specific T cell responses. These survival benefits were subsequently confirmed in mice treated with a highly specific DP1 receptor antagonist, Asapiprant, which is currently being tested in phase II clinical trials. In our new preliminary studies, we have confirmed this age-related immune dysfunction pathway also exists in metastatic lung tumor-bearing mice. Specifically, we have found that PLA2G2D or DP1 deficiency, very effectively restricts the growth of melanoma lung metastasis in a manner that correlates with a substantial early enrichment of γδ-T cells. In this phase 2 CCII COBRE project, we hypothesize that PLA2G2D/PGD2-DP1 signaling contributes to primary and metastatic tumor growth in the lung and acts by inhibiting age-associated inflammasome activation in lung DCs. To test this hypothesis, we will: 1) Determine the mechanisms and signaling effectors underlying PLA2G2D/PGD2-DP1 signaling in lung DCs from aged, tumor bearing mice, and 2) Investigate the potential of the DP1-targeting small molecule, Asapiprant, as a potential mono-immunotherapy in treating clinically relevant lung primary and metastatic disease models. Finally, these studies will evaluate whether DP1 targeting in immune checkpoint blockade (ICB) resistant implantable and spontaneous tumor models is sufficient to reduce resistance/increase efficacy in combination with anti-PD-1.

title: The role of phosphatidic acid in liver regeneration after acetaminophen overdose
text:
This project is important for public health because it will lay the foundation for better treatments for liver injury.
Acute liver failure is a devastating illness with limited treatment options. This project will improve understanding
of natural, endogenous repair processes in the liver so we can exploit them to improve patient outcomes.

title: Role of LAM-specific TREM1 in leukemogenesis
text:
Cancer progression is heavily influenced by supportive cells in the tumor microenvironment. The project aims to
investigate the previously unknown connection between TREM1-positive leukemia-associated macrophages
(LAMs) and leukemogenesis. If successfully completed, the project would uncover novel roles of TREM1 in LAM-
leukemia interaction during leukemia development, and yield valuable information on whether targeting TREM1
or its signaling components may be therapeutically useful in the prevention and treatment of leukemia.

title: A new paradigm of glomerular immune cell homing
text:
Relevance
Inflammatory kidney diseases such as glomerulonephritis, diabetic kidney disease and lupus nephritis
are associated with significant comorbidities and mortalities and affect close to a third of the US
population, yet their pathophysiology remains incompletely understood. Macula densa cells play pivotal
roles in the maintenance of the normal structure and function of the healthy glomerulus and also in the
development of glomerular injury in kidney diseases, yet their primary immunomodulatory role has been
largely overlooked. We propose to study the role of macula densa cells and their pro and anti-
inflammatory function in the normal and diseased kidney, and to develop new therapeutic approaches
for inflammatory kidney diseases.

title: Gene regulatory programs underlying differences in neural crest developmental potential in the head and neck
text:
The neural crest of the head and neck contributes to many essential tissues including the craniofacial
skeleton, parts of the cardiac mesenchyme, and the enteric nervous system. The ability of the neural
crest to form ectomesenchymal tissue, such as craniofacial cartilage, is lost in lower parts of the body.
Further study of the gene regulatory differences that establish these differential cell fates will inform
our understanding of the neural crest while carrying potential implications for underlying craniofacial
birth defects and regenerative therapies targeted at generation of ectomesenchyme tissue.

title: Dissecting the immunomodulatory effects of NK cells on immune responses to cancer
text:
Our previous studies identified Natural Killer (NK) cells as important regulators of the immune response to cancer
and responses to current FDA-approved immunotherapies. This research proposal will define novel cellular and
molecular pathways that regulate the immunomodulatory effects of NK cells in the tumor microenvironment. This
project will be the first steps towards the development of novel immunotherapies that harness the
immunomodulatory effects of NK cells to increase patient’s immune responses to cancer.
